messages:
maya: seeing a spike of 5xx / timeouts against hosted inference API (/v1/generate) starting ~10:12 PST. Datadog SLO alert: API-Gateway-5xx-Timeout-SLO triggered. latency p95 jumped, and error budget is burning fast. :fire:
opsbot: PagerDuty incident INC-20260315-72 created, assigned to oncall-sre.
john: on it. first glance — 502s + 504s, but traces are sparse for the failed requests. appears to be gateway timeouts when backend model pods are returning slow.
anika: can you paste the datadog monitor link and the query? I want to check which AZ/region this hits.
maya: monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/9876543210 (API-Gateway-5xx-Timeout-SLO). Query used: 
```
avg(last_5m):sum:apigateway.requests{env:prod,status:5xx}.as_count() / sum:apigateway.requests{env:prod}.as_count() > 0.02
```
Also running log query in Kibana:
```
POST /_search
{ "query": { "bool": { "must": [ { "match": { "path": "/v1/generate" } }, { "range": { "@timestamp": { "gte": "now-15m" } } }, { "match": { "status": "5xx" } } ] } } }
```
Found many entries with 504 and a short stack: `gateway/proxy.go:142 -> context deadline exceeded` and backend trace ids like `trace=7b1f2a1c` but the tracing collector didn't ingest spans for those trace ids.
leo: missing spans often means the backend failed before emitting spans or the sampling dropped them. Could be overload in model-serving lane. Any autoscaler events?
john: checking k8s events — HPA bumped pods up then throttled, OOMs on a few pods (gpu-worker-*) around 10:05-10:09. Node pressure in us-west-2c.
anika: if nodes hit memory pressure, kubelet evicted pods which causes transient 5xx while the gateway waits. That matches the errors.
maya: support thread from a customer (enterprise) came in complaining about their jobs failing with 502s and we promised an update. Need mitigation asap.
opsbot: Running mitigation runbook: fallback to smaller model tier.
john: rolling a temporary routing policy to divert 20% of traffic to redwood-mini in us-west-2 while we stabilize. Command: 
```
rbctl routing set --env prod --region us-west-2 --route /v1/generate --policy "fallback_model=redwood-mini,traffic_shift=0.2"
```
maya: will that increase latency for those 20%? we should warn customers if quality differs.
john: small impact but acceptable short-term; we're notifying support.
anika: also bump the node pool max size + disable aggressive binpacking for gpu nodes. kubectl patch cluster autoscaler will be used.
leo: I'm going to run a targeted log aggregation for the failing trace ids to check upstream latencies:
```
index=apigw logs | where path=="/v1/generate" and status>=500 and timestamp >= now()-30m | stats count() by backend_host, status
```
maya: repro steps from support to validate: curl example with JWT header that reproduces 504 after ~15s:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"long-running test"}' --max-time 30
```
When running locally I see a 200 if we hit a healthy pod, 504 if routed to a restarting pod.
support-bot: Customer-facing incident created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-8942 — status: investigating.
maya: question — could this be related to a recent rollout? I saw a canary of model-serving runtime yesterday.
john: checked rollout timeline. A canary push to runtime v1.42 happened at 02:30 UTC, but full rollout paused. No obvious correlation. More likely resource pressure and a bad combination of large batch sizes + memory regression in new model quantization path.
leo: tracing gaps: our collector has ~1.2% dropped spans for this window, but dropped spans alone shouldn't account for missing root spans. Backend service logs show process restarts.
anika: mitigation checklist I propose: 1) hold canary and roll back model-quantization patch if suspicious; 2) increase node pool capacity and set pod disruption budget adjustments; 3) route some traffic to fallback model (done); 4) temporarily increase gateway upstream timeout to 35s for critical customers; 5) notify support + update CS ticket.
john: implementing 2) and 4) now. Gateway timeout change (datadog dashboard + config): 
```
rbctl gateway update --timeout 35s --path /v1/generate --env prod
```
maya: after routing change and node pool bump, 5xx rate already dropping in the last 3 minutes. SLO burn rate slowed.
opsbot: Incident INC-20260315-72: status changed to "mitigated" by john at 10:28 PST.
maya: follow-ups: we need a post-incident action item: improve trace sampling on gateway retries, add a monitor for OOMs on gpu-worker nodes, and add a deploy-time checklist to stress-test quantization changes on staging.
anika: I'll own the OOM monitor. putting a follow-up ticket: SRE-3120.
leo: engineering action — add a fallback circuit breaker so the gateway instantly fails over to dedicated fallback model if backend latency crosses threshold. I'll draft a design doc.
maya: for support: recommend telling affected customers we're investigating and that we routed some traffic to a lower-latency fallback; engineering will follow up with RCA in ~24 hours.
support-bot: update sent to CS ticket CS-8942: "Mitigated — temporary routing applied, autoscaler increased. Engineering investigating root cause."
john: leaving logs/queries I used for RCA in the incident runbook gist: https://gist.github.com/john/incident-runs-1845001234
maya: great work, team. I'll schedule a 30-min post-incident sync at 15:00 UTC to capture RCA notes and next steps. :calendar:
